programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid a’ còcaireachd cuide ri a caraidean. An-diugh tha Rowan agus Calum Fraser cuide rithe agus iad a’ deasachadh risotto le feòil-circe agus piobar dearg. Ach mus tòisich iad a’ còcaireachd, feumaidh iad dèanamh cinnteach gu bheil na tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, nì iad liosta agus thèid iad dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach cò às a tha peasairean a’ tighinn. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson an risotto a dhèanamh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe! Linda is joined by Rowan and Calum Fraser to make a delicious risotto with chicken and red peppers. But first they must ensure they have all the ingredients and, if not, they make a list and go shopping. They also learn more about where peas come from, and then it’s back to the kitchen to prepare the risotto before sitting down to eat!

programme.title: Oscar & Ealasaid
programme.desc: Tha seanamhair Oscar a’ tighinn air chèilidh, agus tha Oscar is Ealasaid airson bòrd a chur air dòigh ann an taigh-bìdh air a bheiI i glè eòlach. Ach, airson biadh òrdanachadh ann an àite cho spaideil, feumar modh ionnsachadh. Ernest's grandmother, Baboutchinka, has come to visit. To surprise her, Ernest and Célestine want to reserve a table at a restaurant that she knows well. But in order to eat at such a fancy place, one must have good manners!

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Àtaidh a’ dèanamh aran brochain, ach tha e a’ fàilleachdainn air an reasabaidh fhaighinn ceart. Dè nì e leis na tha e air a dhèanamh de dh’aran? Abney is making Porridge bread, but he just can't get the recipe right. What will he do with all these spare loaves?

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha e a' còrdadh ri na h-Abadas a bhith a' cluich le bàll air a' chladach, gus a bheil gaoth làidir a' sèideadh am bàll a-muigh gu muir! Tha na h-Abadas ag ionnsachadh nach e 'bàll' an aon rud a bhios a' gluasad sa ghaoth. The Abadas are enjoying a game of ball at the seaside until the strong winds blow the ball out to sea! The Abadas soon find out that a ball isn't the only thing that moves in the wind.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha an Teaghlach Rìoghail air gluasad an ath-dhoras ’s tha Stella airson a h-obair-sgoile a sgrùdadh le Mìcheal agus tha an Rìgh agus a’ Bhànrigh a’ dol a-mach air deit. The royal family have moved next door, Stella wants to revise schoolwork with Mìcheal, and the King and Queen are going on a date.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha caraidean Stella ri tadhal an-diugh agus tha i airson dearbhadh gu bheil iad àbhaisteach – dìreach mar a h-uile duine eile! Stella’s friends visit today, and she wants to prove that they are normal, just like everyone else!

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: Chaidh an MV Hallaig a chuir air bhog ann an 2012 agus aig an àm, b’ i a’ chiad aiseig hybrid san t-saoghal. Tha Calum air latha a chuir seachad air bòrd airson faighinn a-mach ciamar a tha siostam hybrid ag obair. The MV Hallaig was launched in 2012 and at that time, she was the only hybrid ferry in the world. Calum spends a day on board to find out exactly how this hybrid system works.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha tòrr rudan a’ dèanamh sgrios air a’ choille, mar eisimpleir daolagan rùisg, gnàth-shìde, ‘s tha Mika draghail oir ’s ann o chraobhan a bhios sinn a’ faighinn ar n-ogsaidean. Ri linn sin, tha Mika airson craobhan a chur ’s an coille a shàbhaladh. Many things are destroying the forest, for example bark beetles and climate change and, as we draw our oxygen from trees, Mika is worried. As a result of this, Mika wants to save the forest by planting trees.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Beloved Wilderness
programme.desc: Documentary examining the work of the Highlands and Islands Development Board during the 1960s, originally aired in 1970.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Tha an Lof Banana aig Abigail gu math sònraichte aig àm brunch, agus a’ sàsachadh a’ chàil. An dearbh bhiadh airson a ghabhail le càirdean is caraidean. Abigail’s banana loaf is a very special and tasty brunch experience, satisfying to the extreme and just the thing to share with family and friends. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Co-Sheirm
programme.desc: Sreath bhon tasglann a' taisbeanadh còisirean is guthan sònraichte. An t-seachdain-sa, Còisir Ghàidhlig Inbhir Nis. Archive series featuring choirs and outstanding soloists from The Inverness Gaelic Choir.

programme.title: Mach à Seo!
programme.desc: Ramsay travels through Caithness for a busy and exhilarating few days. Lathaichean trang agus inntinneach do Ramsay a’ siubhal tro Ghallaibh.

programme.title: Suas gu Deas
programme.desc: Tha aifreann nan iasgair ann am Barraigh agus show Uibhist a Tuath ann a Homhstadh. The fisherman’s mass is held on Castlebay pier and it’s a busy day at the North Uist show.

programme.title: Port Steòrnabhaigh
programme.desc: Based in the main port in the Hebrides, we follow the beating heart of Stornoway Harbour. In her shelter, there is a bustling community to be found. In this episode, a cruise ship is safely piloted into Stornoway, and we meet artists who make the very most of treasures washed ashore. Stèidhte ann am prìomh port nan Eilean Siar, the sinne a’ leantainn cridhe Port Steòrnabhaigh. Na fasgadh, tha coimhearsnachd trang ri lorg. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha bàta-crùis air a stiùireadh a-steach a Phort Steòrnabhaigh gu sàbhailte, ‘s coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-ealain comasach a tha a’ cleachdach toradh a’ chladaich. Thig còmhla rinn ‘s sinn a’ leanntainn beatha ann am Port Steòrnabhaigh.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram ciùil air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Chaidh Seirm Celtic Connections a chlàradh ann an ionad Platform ann an Glaschu ann a 2022 le feadhainn den luchd-ciùil as fheàrr bho air feadh a R.A. agus às na S.A. Anns an darna prògram roghainneach seo gheibhear taghadh de cheòl dùthchasach agus traidiseanta bho’n Ciaran Ryan Band, Trials of Cato, Màiri Nic a’ Mhaoilein agus a còmhlan agus Jarrod Dickenson. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Seirm Celtic Connections was filmed in 2022 during the festival in Platform, Glasgow. Appearing are a cross section of musicians from the UK and the US. This programme reflects the diversity of the festival with appearances by the Ciaran Ryan Band, Trials of Cato, Màiri MacMillan and band, plus Jarrod Dickenson. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Jock Stein
programme.desc: 'S ann à Baile beag ann an Siorrachd Lannraig a thàinig am manaidsear as fheàrr a bh' ann an Alba a-riamh. 'S e sgeulachd a' mhèinneir, an duine fhèin agus curaidh ball-coise a th' ann an "JOCK STEIN", fear dhe na h-ainmean as cliùitiche ann am ball-coise na cruinne. A working class miner from a small village in Lanarkshire became Scotland's greatest ever football manager and one of the biggest names in world football. 'Jock Stein' is the story of the miner, the man, and the football legend.

programme.title: Sgeulachd Cogaidh na h-Artaig/Untold Arctic Wars
programme.desc: Deep mistrust exists between the two sides. The Soviet Union threatens with neutron bombs, and Nato deploys missiles in Europe.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Ellie Beaton a’ gabhail a-steach A Miner’s Life agus It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by Ellie Beaton featuring the songs, A Miner’s Life and It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le taisbeanadh air leth bho Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House aig Belladrum 2025 is an còmhlan cliùiteach Albannach, Texas, a’ tilleadh chun na fèise mar phrìomh chòmhlan oidhche Shathairne. Le fuaim leantaileach is guth iongantach Sharleen Spiteri, tha an còmhlan a’ toirt thugainn na h-òrain as fheàrr aca, ’s chan eil leisg air an t-sluagh seinn còmhla riutha. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain MacDonald present from the Hot House Stage at Belladrum as iconic Scottish band Texas return to the festival to headline Saturday night. With their timeless sound and Sharleen Spiteri’s unmistakable vocals, the group perform classic hits, and the crowd need no encouragement to join in.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Jamie Theakston presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 10 December 1999 and featuring Whitney Houston, Mario Piu, Jamiroquai, Celine Dion, Artful Dodger feat Craig David, Atomic Kitten and Cliff Richard.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Paul Burnett presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 31 May 1979 and featuring Quantum Jump, Chas & Dave, Sparks, Fischer-Z, Peaches & Herb, Voyager, Blondie and Hot Chocolate. With a dance sequence from Legs & Co.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Anthea Turner and Gary Davies present the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 1 June 1989 and featuring Sinitta, Fuzzbox and Neneh Cherry.

programme.title: Aretha Franklin at the BBC
programme.desc: Aretha Franklin is widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest singers of all time, and yet more proof of that can be found in this collection of her performances on BBC programmes from across the decades. From a stunning 2015 performance of You Make Me Feel (Like a Natural Woman) that had President Barack Obama in tears to gems from the 1970s, when Aretha dropped in to be the guest star on shows hosted by Cliff Richard and Lulu, these songs and her voice will remind everyone why she is still to this day considered the ultimate queen of soul.

programme.desc: During the final months of WWII, a remote Alpine village hosts a Sicilian deserter, who has a profound effect on the quiet, everyday lives of the devout Graziadei family - especially the daughters.

programme.title: Butterflies
programme.desc: Ria has enough to cope with: there is her husband Ben, who has his own hang-ups and her sons Adam and Russell, who are the cause of most of them. Then suddenly there's Leonard.

programme.title: Artsnight
programme.desc: Carla Lane redefined British comedy drama in the 1970s with her unique brand of 'situation tragedy'. At a time when television writing was the preserve of middle-class men, she brought a convincing cast of working-class female characters to British screens. The daring honesty with which she told the stories of ordinary women revolutionised the roles available to actresses on TV and blazed a trail for the screenwriters following in her footsteps. This special edition of Artsnight delves into the BBC's archive and brings together rarely seen interviews in which writer Carla Lane discusses her life and work, while Carla's son Carl offers personal insights into his mother's career and legacy. With contributions from the Liver Birds - Polly James and Nerys Hughes - and Geoffrey Palmer, the long-suffering husband to Ria in Butterflies.

programme.desc: Harriet Bradshaw finds out how AI is being used to help solve an art history mystery. Nick Kwek visits the University of Texas to explore new innovations in hydrogen car technology. Andrew Rogers heads behind the scenes of Pinewood Studios. And Paul Carter meets the robodog helping to analyse plants and crops.

programme.title: Rachel Khoo's Kitchen Notebook
programme.desc: Rachel explores this quirky vibrant Spanish city taking in its creativity as she indulges in a traditional chocolaty breakfast and finds a kitchen with a modern take on tapas. Rachel is particularly inspired by the Spanish sweet doughnut churros and by the city's food market. Back home in London, Rachel cooks up savoury churros with a roasted red pepper dipping sauce and some chocolate and fig truffles.

programme.title: On the Front Line
programme.desc: Reports of sexual assault and harassment on trains and at stations are on the rise, but victims say CCTV cameras are often broken or of such poor quality that their attackers can't be identified. We follow British Transport Police officers and staff as they race against time to gather the crucial evidence they need to bring offenders to justice.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: A new Netflix documentary follows the final stage of Rafael Nadal's tennis career. The series is the latest high-profile sports documentary made for a streaming platform. Zachary Heinzerling, director of Rafa, outlines how the film was made and the level of access his team received. Minal Modha, senior research director at Ampere Analysis, provides context on the growing business of sports documentaries. In Scotland, Peter Murrell's guilty plea to embezzling funds from the SNP has renewed attention on the reporting that first raised questions about the affair. John Ferguson, political editor at the Sunday Mail, reflects on his own journalism. Laura Kuenssberg explains how she secured the first broadcast interview with Nicola Sturgeon since her estranged husband's conviction. CBS News is facing upheaval following changes in leadership and the departure of several senior figures. The latest developments centre on the dismissal of veteran correspondent Scott Pelley after public criticism of the network's direction. Michael Grynbaum, media correspondent at The New York Times, outlines the story.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: The traditional French bistro is mounting a comeback. In recent times, an average of 25 a day have been shutting their doors, as eating habits change across France. Now though, efforts are underway to save them. Briony May Williams travels through the south of the country to find out what this casual form of dining has brought to French culture. She heads to a village that's finally about to reopen a bistro that it lost many years ago, and explores the rowdy breakfast culture of Lyon's Machon cafes.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: The FIFA 2026 World Cup will be the biggest ever — spanning three countries, 48 teams, 104 matches, and an audience of billions. Now, for the first time, artificial intelligence will sit at the heart of the tournament. From sharper offside decisions to real-time digital replicas of all 16 stadiums, organisers will use AI to monitor crowds, improve safety, and manage the event from a single command centre. For fans, both in the stadium and at home, it promises an entirely new way to experience the game. So will more AI really improve the game? Or risk taking something away from it? AI Decoded explores whether technology can truly enhance football — and what fans actually want from the future of the sport.

Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: Mrs Brown's Boys actor Eilish O'Carroll joins Anna to explore their native Dublin. They celebrate the old and discover the new in their changing city, including a visit to the iconic Guinness factory, where brewing began in 1759. Inspired by the visit, Anna cooks with her mum, evoking childhood memories. Eilish also takes Anna to Moore Street, where traditional markets mix with global street food. The pair later cook a dish inspired by the city's diverse flavours.

Meanwhile, Danny has an intriguing mystery item to perplex fairgoers.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After 15 years living and working in Dubai, two expats want to return home to the UK and need Sonali Shah’s help to find them a new home in wonderful West Sussex. Sonali also drops in on a farm that specialises in growing a variety of sunflowers, many of which are taller than she is!

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo are in Egham to transform Neil and Rumen's overgrown and unloved plot into an Islamic-themed garden. They would love a sophisticated space that echoes some of their travels, particularly their trips to the Middle East. Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Blankety Blank
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as a panel of six celebrities fill in the missing blanks and help win brilliant prizes for some very lucky contestants. This time, he’s joined by Chris McCausland, Emmett J Scanlan, Melvin Odoom, Sue Perkins, Grace Dent and Vanessa Williams.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: A special comedy edition of the general knowledge quiz in which four teams try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and co-host Richard Osman, with contestants Olga Koch, Chloe Petts, Arabella Weir, Jon Culshaw, Ted Robbins, Justin Moorhouse, Neil Delamere and Loyiso Gola.

programme.title: The Weakest Link
programme.desc: BAFTA-award-winning comedian Romesh Ranganathan is back hosting one of the world’s most iconic quizzes. Eight celebrities must initially work together to bank as much money as possible for charity, before voting off one player per round as the weakest link. Only one player will be crowned the strongest link and will take home the prize for their charity. Celebrity contestants in this episode are Mel B, Eamonn Holmes, Shobna Gulati, Denis Lawson, Arielle Free, Briony May Williams, Nick Pickard and Rob Bent.

programme.title: Casualty
programme.desc: Will Flynn be able to stop history repeating itself?

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: Zoe feels liberated at a ‘Gods and Monsters’ party hosted by eccentric local expats Flick and James, while Dan spirals into a dark place back at the villa. News of their separation unsettles each of the friends as the party takes unexpected turns. The frisson between Zoe and Solomon becomes undeniable. Avery is drawn to Jon, Jacob goes on an unexpected sexual odyssey, and Nat blows up her life. When Zoe listens to what her visions might be telling her, will she go too far?

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: Mrs Brown's Boys actor Eilish O'Carroll joins Anna to explore their native Dublin. They celebrate the old and discover the new in their changing city, including a visit to the iconic Guinness factory, where brewing began in 1759. Inspired by the visit, Anna cooks with her mum, evoking childhood memories. Eilish also takes Anna to Moore Street, where traditional markets mix with global street food. The pair later cook a dish inspired by the city's diverse flavours.

programme.desc: After 15 years living and working in Dubai, two expats want to return home to the UK and need Sonali Shah’s help to find them a new home in wonderful West Sussex. Sonali also drops in on a farm that specialises in growing a variety of sunflowers, many of which are taller than she is!

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo are in Egham to transform Neil and Rumen's overgrown and unloved plot into an Islamic-themed garden. They would love a sophisticated space that echoes some of their travels, particularly their trips to the Middle East. Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Garden Rescue

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Charlie and Flo are in Egham to transform Neil and Rumen's overgrown and unloved plot into an Islamic-themed garden. They would love a sophisticated space that echoes some of their travels, particularly their trips to the Middle East. Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: On a mission to dig out some of his greatest adventures from the past, Derek revisits three memorable walks from mid-Wales. On his first wander, he is joined by opera singer Beverley Humphreys as they walk in the footsteps of one of history’s most impressive sopranos at the Craig-y-Nos estate. He learns of the epic barefoot 26-mile journey of a devoted teenage girl in Abergynolwyn. Finally, Derek takes the plunge at the World Bog Snorkelling Championship in Llanwrtyd Wells.

Avery is drawn to Jon, Jacob goes on an unexpected sexual odyssey, and Nat blows up her life. When Zoe listens to what her visions might be telling her, will she go too far?

All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop

Can he bring back the stage, the iconic mural and the heartbeat of a vanished community?

Meanwhile, Danny has an intriguing mystery item to perplex fairgoers.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: A smashed-up wardrobe poses a carpentry conundrum for Bruce. Can he hammer, saw and smash his way to perfection?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After 15 years living and working in Dubai, two expats want to return home to the UK and need Sonali Shah’s help to find them a new home in wonderful West Sussex. Sonali also drops in on a farm that specialises in growing a variety of sunflowers, many of which are taller than she is!

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo are in Egham to transform Neil and Rumen's overgrown and unloved plot into an Islamic-themed garden. They would love a sophisticated space that echoes some of their travels, particularly their trips to the Middle East. Can the team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring Olympian and TV presenter Greg Rutherford, comedian and actor Sanjeev Kohli, presenter and writer Janet Ellis and actor Louisa Lytton as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Blankety Blank
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as a panel of six celebrities fill in the missing blanks and help win brilliant prizes for some very lucky contestants. This time, he’s joined by Chris McCausland, Emmett J Scanlan, Melvin Odoom, Sue Perkins, Grace Dent and Vanessa Williams.

programme.title: Pointless Celebrities
programme.desc: A special comedy edition of the general knowledge quiz in which four teams try to come up with the answers that no-one else could think of. Presented by Alexander Armstrong and co-host Richard Osman, with contestants Olga Koch, Chloe Petts, Arabella Weir, Jon Culshaw, Ted Robbins, Justin Moorhouse, Neil Delamere and Loyiso Gola.

programme.title: The Weakest Link
programme.desc: BAFTA-award-winning comedian Romesh Ranganathan is back hosting one of the world’s most iconic quizzes. Eight celebrities must initially work together to bank as much money as possible for charity, before voting off one player per round as the weakest link. Only one player will be crowned the strongest link and will take home the prize for their charity. Celebrity contestants in this episode are Mel B, Eamonn Holmes, Shobna Gulati, Denis Lawson, Arielle Free, Briony May Williams, Nick Pickard and Rob Bent.

programme.title: Casualty
programme.desc: Will Flynn be able to stop history repeating itself?

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: Zoe feels liberated at a ‘Gods and Monsters’ party hosted by eccentric local expats Flick and James, while Dan spirals into a dark place back at the villa. News of their separation unsettles each of the friends as the party takes unexpected turns. The frisson between Zoe and Solomon becomes undeniable. Avery is drawn to Jon, Jacob goes on an unexpected sexual odyssey, and Nat blows up her life. When Zoe listens to what her visions might be telling her, will she go too far?

programme.title: Love in the Flesh
programme.desc: Five online couples meet in the flesh for the first time to spend a week together in a glorious Greek beach house. Will the online spark translate into the real world?

programme.title: Love in the Flesh
programme.desc: It’s day two in the beach house where our five couples are navigating their way through a real-life relationship. After meeting for the first time in the flesh yesterday, these pairings are either on the way up or looking unlikely to last the week. The couples go on their first dates with no screens or filters to hide behind. Zara announces that there are two private suites and that it’s up to the group to decide who should spend the night in them and why. Tension builds when one of the housemates reveals her head has been turned by another of the men in the beach house, and her online partner is left feeling crushed. Will she act on her desires or stay true to the man she has built an online bond with?

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s big comedy talent search heads north to Newcastle. The venue is The Boiler Shop, a stunning Grade II listed industrial building. Five comics battle it out to book their place in this year’s grand final showdown, where one will be crowned the BBC New Comedian of 2025. Hosting the evening is comic, writer and actor Amy Gledhill. Judging their performances are writer and star of Smoggie Queens Phil Dunning and 2022 NCA winner Dan Tiernan, plus head judge Fatiha El-Ghorri. Charlie Ashton, Murph, Zoe Cousin, Ciara O’Connor and Shugufta Choudhry each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final at Bradford’s Alhambra Theatre.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Stay-at-home-daughter Chi is suddenly forced to fend for herself when her parents die in a car crash. Chi learns she will only inherit the house on condition she completes a list of 'Things You Should Have Done' left in the parents' will, the first of which is, ironically, learn to drive. Meanwhile, Chi's highly strung auntie Karen wants nothing to do with her dependent pest of a niece, but very much wants the house she feels is rightfully hers. Chi ventures out into Ramsgate in search of a driving license and infiltrates the family of a mild-mannered driving instructor in the process.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi spectacularly fails a trial period at the pharmacy with Karen, but Dave kindly lets her shadow him on his delivery rounds. On a drop-off to a retirement home, Chi finds her tribe... old people. She also falls in love with Linda, an elderly lady who seems to think Chi is her husband. Elsewhere, Dave has a health scare, and Karen starts to think she might be the fertility issue.

programme.desc: One morning in every city and town in the world, the human race wakes up to face the most surprising invasion yet. programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda and Penny are forced into therapy for an assessment. How will they cope when trapped in a room together for a half-hour session with an unnervingly silent therapist? All they have to do is sit quietly and control themselves. Testing times for any mother and daughter, let alone Miranda and Penny.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: It's Christmas and Miranda, for once, would like a relaxing and fun time without her parents. After Penny's Best Christmas Jumper Party on the 23rd of December (it's even more humiliating than it sounds) Miranda and Stevie try to spend Christmas at the shop with Gary, Clive and Tilly. What could possibly go wrong? Well, after the online present shopping doesn't arrive, the infuriating encounter at the post office (is there anything more annoying than a 'we tried to deliver but you were out' card?), a run-in with some carol singers and a couple of arguments with friends, maybe Christmas would be better with her family.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: This New Year is all about reconciliation and fresh starts in the Brown household, but not everyone seems to have got the message. Grandad’s brother Mickey is fresh out of prison and decides to stop by for a visit. Everyone except Grandad is suspicious when he shows up asking for 5,000 euros to invest in a South African gold mine. Winnie, inspired by Cathy’s book, is on a daredevil mission to change the trajectory of her life, while Mrs Brown’s boys are forced to have a heart to heart.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: SV2 and Manny celebrate the World Cup on Blue Peter with skills, tricks and iconic goal recreations! The footballing duo go head-to-head as they take on challenges and look at legendary World Cup moments – don’t miss it!

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Roses are stealing the spotlight at Longmeadow, and Monty is celebrating all the full, head-turning bloom. From richly scented classics to vibrant modern varieties, this is peak rose season - a chance to see them at their absolute best and solve some common problems. With planting in full swing across borders and beds, there are annuals and exotics to deal with, and in the veg plot, it’s time to plant lettuce and beetroots. Ashley Edwards visits Benton End, a place of artistic vision and horticultural legacy, to see a historic collection of bearded irises beloved by Cedric Morris. In Penarth, Sue Kent uncovers a rich mix of gardens, personalities and inspiration. A cleverly designed city garden in Brighton, packed with personality and planting inspiration, proves that small spaces can deliver big impact. Meanwhile, in Bedfordshire, one gardener has embraced a very different climate – filling his space with striking succulents and sun-loving plants to create a garden with a distinctly exotic edge.

programme.title: Great Expectations (1946)
programme.desc: A vivid adaptation of Charles Dickens's classic novel from master director David Lean. The simple life of a poor orphan is forever altered after a chance encounter with a fearsome criminal and the intervention of a mysterious benefactor. In line with the wishes of the wealthy stranger, the boy is taken to London, where he is introduced to a higher class of society and transformed into a gentleman. Despite his new riches however, he is unable to win over the object of his affections - a beautiful but spoilt young woman he has known since childhood. Lean's vivid version of the tale won Academy Awards for cinematography and art direction.

programme.title: The Wooden Horse
programme.desc: Dramatisation of one of the most ingenious escape bids of World War II. In camp Stalag Luft III, the Nazis have built the prisoners' huts so far from the fence that underground escape is virtually impossible. One British officer, inspired by the tale of the Trojan Horse, proposes a daring plan to start a tunnel close to the boundary using a wooden vaulting horse as cover.

programme.title: Ice Station Zebra
programme.desc: When a secret film capsule from a Russian spacecraft lands near Station Zebra, the tiny weather base is plunged into the Cold War and a confrontation between two super powers.

programme.title: Rugby League: Super League
programme.desc: Wakefield face Hull KR in the 2026 Super League.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From Charles Paget Wade's collection of samurai armour in Snowshill Manor to the Harpur-Crewe family's immense natural history collection at Calke Abbey, this episode explores the remarkable world of collectors – and the dedicated National Trust teams working to protect their extraordinary legacies of curious collectibles, rare wildlife and living heritage.

programme.title: Weather Hits at the BBC
programme.desc: An unpredictable but joyous collection of weather-related chart hits, courtesy of two of the BBC’s most formidable forecasters, Carol Kirkwood and Tomasz Schafernaker. It’s a selection that covers all conditions, from Ain’t No Sunshine When She’s Gone, to Why Does It Always Rain on Me, sprinkled throughout with fun facts and crucial context from Carol and Tomasz - clearly relishing this chance to step away from weather charts and test out the music charts.

programme.title: The Game - The Story of Hurling
programme.desc: Born in a haze of myths and legends, this episode explores the birth of hurling and the hurler. Ulster warrior Cú Chulainn is a key figure in its iconography, and today, the Poc Fada competition follows his trail across the Cooley Mountains. And what does hurling mean to the island as a whole? Where does it lie in history and Ireland’s unfolding identities? Charting the formation of the GAA alongside the turbulent times of the Land War and mass emigration, this episode explores the groundwork on which a remarkable sport was founded. Whether it’s the ultimate dream of representing your county in Croke Park on finals day or the tribal pride of playing for club or parish, picking up a hurl and sliotar brings a true sense of belonging to something much bigger.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: It’s fair to say that when it comes to classic national dishes, the French and British like to do things differently. However, both have a passion for poisson. Forty-five per cent of French households eat fish at least once a week, and Marcus wants to find out what kind of fish they like and if there’s a French dish to rival the great British fish and chips. If there's one fruit that might be even more synonymous with Provence than garlic, it's the olive. They’ve been grown here for over 3,500 years, and Marcus wants to understand the region’s passion for these tiny, versatile delights.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition of the antiques series comes from the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Michael Baggott and Anita Manning find some real gems among the bags and boxes to take to auction. There's a fascinating pair of beaded gloves and an amber necklace which takes the saleroom by storm. And Paul Martin explores the history of one of Britain's few remaining Palladian houses.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nikki Fox, Ruthie Henshall, Danny John-Jules and Ignacio Lopez take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Blankety Blank
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as a panel of six celebrities fill in the missing blanks and help win brilliant prizes for some very lucky contestants. This time, he’s joined by Chris McCausland, Emmett J Scanlan, Melvin Odoom, Sue Perkins, Grace Dent and Vanessa Williams.

programme.title: Springwatch in Wales
programme.desc: Iolo Williams presents the best stories of Welsh rivers from Springwatch. At RSPB Ynys-hir, Iolo recalls the delights of fledging dippers and courting kingfishers. He canoes through the Cilgerran Gorge on the Teifi, while Dewi Roberts likes nothing better than snorkelling in the Wye, sharing his passion for the tiny creatures that live beneath the surface. Chris Packham revels in the love triangle involving Monty, the most famous osprey on the Dyfi, and two females vying for his attention and his nest. Finally, cameraman Robin Smith paddles down the Wye to find the best places to mount his camera traps – to record otter, fox and much more that lives along its banks.

programme.title: Coast
programme.desc: Coast visits Loch Creran on the Scottish west coast, where industrious little worms have constructed a remarkable 'worm city' that is one of the biggest of its kind in the world.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 3 highlights from the Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Casualty
programme.desc: Will Flynn be able to stop history repeating itself?

programme.title: In My Own Words
programme.desc: In an intimate and heartfelt interview, Britain’s biggest voice, Sir Tom Jones, reflects on his extraordinary life and stellar career in song. From his proud working-class roots in the Welsh valleys to music’s most glittering stages and the world’s television sets, Tom’s remarkable journey spans more than 80 years – and it’s still going strong. But it has not always been easy, and it has required a constant balancing act between fame and fortune, family and staying true to the gift he was born with. This poignant programme reveals the man behind the voice as Tom looks back on the joy and pain of life and loss. Featuring rare archive footage Tom has never seen before and visits to the places that mean the most to him, it’s a moving portrait of a national treasure.

programme.title: Tom Jones at the BBC
programme.desc: An archive celebration of Tom Jones's performances at the BBC from the start of his pop career in the mid-60s to Later... with Jools Holland in 2010 and all points in between, including Top of the Pops and The Dusty Springfield Show. A chronological celebration of Sir Tom through the years that is also a history of music TV at the BBC over most of the past 50 years.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: From the mighty grizzly bear to the endearing real life Paddington, the spectacled bear, and Rudyard Kipling’s Jungle Book's Baloo, the sloth bear, this remarkable animal family has long captured our imagination. As some of the largest animals on earth, they need more than just the 'bare necessities' to survive - especially in today’s ever-changing world. This film explores how bears across the world have overcome the challenges of life - from finding food and raising the cubs to confronting rivals and habitat loss - all thanks to brains, brawn and a remarkable ability to adapt.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition of the antiques series comes from the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Michael Baggott and Anita Manning find some real gems among the bags and boxes to take to auction. There's a fascinating pair of beaded gloves and an amber necklace which takes the saleroom by storm. And Paul Martin explores the history of one of Britain's few remaining Palladian houses.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nikki Fox, Ruthie Henshall, Danny John-Jules and Ignacio Lopez take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Blankety Blank
programme.desc: Bradley Walsh hosts as a panel of six celebrities fill in the missing blanks and help win brilliant prizes for some very lucky contestants. This time, he’s joined by Chris McCausland, Emmett J Scanlan, Melvin Odoom, Sue Perkins, Grace Dent and Vanessa Williams.

programme.title: Springwatch in Wales
programme.desc: Iolo Williams presents the best stories of Welsh rivers from Springwatch. At RSPB Ynys-hir, Iolo recalls the delights of fledging dippers and courting kingfishers. He canoes through the Cilgerran Gorge on the Teifi, while Dewi Roberts likes nothing better than snorkelling in the Wye, sharing his passion for the tiny creatures that live beneath the surface. Chris Packham revels in the love triangle involving Monty, the most famous osprey on the Dyfi, and two females vying for his attention and his nest. Finally, cameraman Robin Smith paddles down the Wye to find the best places to mount his camera traps – to record otter, fox and much more that lives along its banks.

programme.title: Coast
programme.desc: Coast visits Loch Creran on the Scottish west coast, where industrious little worms have constructed a remarkable 'worm city' that is one of the biggest of its kind in the world.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 3 highlights from the Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Casualty
programme.desc: Will Flynn be able to stop history repeating itself?

programme.title: In My Own Words
programme.desc: In an intimate and heartfelt interview, Britain’s biggest voice, Sir Tom Jones, reflects on his extraordinary life and stellar career in song. From his proud working-class roots in the Welsh valleys to music’s most glittering stages and the world’s television sets, Tom’s remarkable journey spans more than 80 years – and it’s still going strong. But it has not always been easy, and it has required a constant balancing act between fame and fortune, family and staying true to the gift he was born with. This poignant programme reveals the man behind the voice as Tom looks back on the joy and pain of life and loss. Featuring rare archive footage Tom has never seen before and visits to the places that mean the most to him, it’s a moving portrait of a national treasure.

programme.title: Tom Jones at the BBC
programme.desc: An archive celebration of Tom Jones's performances at the BBC from the start of his pop career in the mid-60s to Later... with Jools Holland in 2010 and all points in between, including Top of the Pops and The Dusty Springfield Show. A chronological celebration of Sir Tom through the years that is also a history of music TV at the BBC over most of the past 50 years.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: From the mighty grizzly bear to the endearing real life Paddington, the spectacled bear, and Rudyard Kipling’s Jungle Book's Baloo, the sloth bear, this remarkable animal family has long captured our imagination. As some of the largest animals on earth, they need more than just the 'bare necessities' to survive - especially in today’s ever-changing world. This film explores how bears across the world have overcome the challenges of life - from finding food and raising the cubs to confronting rivals and habitat loss - all thanks to brains, brawn and a remarkable ability to adapt.

programme.title: Weather Hits at the BBC
programme.desc: An unpredictable but joyous collection of weather-related chart hits, courtesy of two of the BBC’s most formidable forecasters, Carol Kirkwood and Tomasz Schafernaker. It’s a selection that covers all conditions, from Ain’t No Sunshine When She’s Gone, to Why Does It Always Rain on Me, sprinkled throughout with fun facts and crucial context from Carol and Tomasz - clearly relishing this chance to step away from weather charts and test out the music charts.

programme.title: Hey Duggee

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Muffin is playing Grouchy Granny at a garage sale when a real grouchy granny shows up.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After hearing a strange sound, the Squirrels turn to Duggee to help identify its source. programme.desc: The Squirrels see Duggee reading Wonderful Stories about Wise Animals and want to learn about wisdom and how they can become wiser. Thank goodness Duggee is so wise!

At the Walled City Brewery - once Army Barracks during the Troubles - he uncovers a secret local ingredient behind their standout brews. For a fresh perspective, Dermot hits the water with kayak instructor Michelle, paddling the Foyle and taking in the skyline from a whole new angle - equal parts scenic and splashy. Back on land, things get fiery on a double-decker bus-turned-taco joint. At Pyke 'N' Pommes, local legend Kevin Pyke blends bold Mexican flavours with top-notch Irish seafood. Dermot gets hands-on, prepping calamari and building tasty tacos that capture Derry's evolving food scene.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Joining Alan Titchmarsh at Manor Farm are Stephen Tompkinson and West End and Broadway star Kerry Ellis. We go behind the scenes at the Globe Theatre ahead of their summer season, and Queen of Herbs Jekka McVicar says 'I do' with herbs with a romantic tale in time for wedding season. Plus, wine expert Toni Osoba has the very best in summer sparkles, and we hear from one woman who gave up her job as a nurse to become a farmer - and she joins us with three of her impressive Highland cows.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: Ainsley gets cosy in the kitchen with some recipes to warm the cockles of your heart. On his Mediterranean adventures, Ainsley takes a stroll through the historic city of Valletta, and Charlotte Dawson pops in for a taste of Ainsley's warming penne con pollo.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot travels to Letterkenny in Donegal, often called Ireland's 'forgotten county', but quickly discovers a place full of unforgettable people, stories and food. Surrounded by ancient rainforest, he heads into the woods to forage for prized golden chanterelle mushrooms before visiting the renowned Lemon Tree Restaurant, where he learns to make tortellini completely from scratch with one of Donegal's most skilled chefs. Dermot also meets Abdul, a Syrian refugee-turned-honey farmer, who teaches him how to extract honey from the hive and shares traditions from home, including how Syrians enjoy honey with strong coffee and a sweet dish called knaffe. Along the way, Dermot uncovers a county quietly building one of Ireland's most exciting food scenes, shaped by resilience, creativity and a deep connection to the land.

programme.title: Taken 2
programme.desc: Action-packed thriller sequel. Retired CIA agent Bryan Mills invites his teenage daughter Kim and his ex-wife Lenore, who has separated from her second husband, to spend a couple of days in Istanbul where he is working - meanwhile, Murad Krasniqi, the patriarch of the Albanian gang of human trafficking broken by Bryan, seeks revenge for the death of his son and organises another gang to kidnap him and his family. When Kim escapes the abductors, she becomes her family's only hope of survival...

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: Despite Jamie's best efforts on the pitch, his new Italian side are struggling to get a win and stay out of the relegation zone. Things go from bad to worse when the Vardys' lakeside villa is dramatically burgled, leaving the whole family on edge and considering whether to return home. Becky and the kids escape to the mountains for a much-needed change of scenery and time to think clearly about their situation. On a whistle-stop trip back to the UK, Becky and Jamie stage an elaborate photoshoot but also find a quiet moment to make the big decision: whatever happens with the football, they will bring the kids home. On Easter Sunday in Italy, Becky and Jamie reveal their decision to the kids during an Easter Egg hunt to an overwhelming reaction. Shortly after, Becky and Jamie fly the kids back to the UK, arriving home for an emotional reunion with family and friends. But when the season is over, will Jamie be joining them for good or stay in Italy - or will a whole new adventure begin?

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot travels to Letterkenny in Donegal, often called Ireland's 'forgotten county', but quickly discovers a place full of unforgettable people, stories and food. Surrounded by ancient rainforest, he heads into the woods to forage for prized golden chanterelle mushrooms before visiting the renowned Lemon Tree Restaurant, where he learns to make tortellini completely from scratch with one of Donegal's most skilled chefs. Dermot also meets Abdul, a Syrian refugee-turned-honey farmer, who teaches him how to extract honey from the hive and shares traditions from home, including how Syrians enjoy honey with strong coffee and a sweet dish called knaffe. Along the way, Dermot uncovers a county quietly building one of Ireland's most exciting food scenes, shaped by resilience, creativity and a deep connection to the land.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Arriving in Derry at the end of the Causeway Coastal Route, Dermot finds a city rewriting its story, with the River Foyle as its beating heart. At the Walled City Brewery - once Army Barracks during the Troubles - he uncovers a secret local ingredient behind their standout brews. For a fresh perspective, Dermot hits the water with kayak instructor Michelle, paddling the Foyle and taking in the skyline from a whole new angle - equal parts scenic and splashy. Back on land, things get fiery on a double-decker bus-turned-taco joint. At Pyke 'N' Pommes, local legend Kevin Pyke blends bold Mexican flavours with top-notch Irish seafood. Dermot gets hands-on, prepping calamari and building tasty tacos that capture Derry's evolving food scene.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Joining Alan Titchmarsh at Manor Farm are Stephen Tompkinson and West End and Broadway star Kerry Ellis. We go behind the scenes at the Globe Theatre ahead of their summer season, and Queen of Herbs Jekka McVicar says 'I do' with herbs with a romantic tale in time for wedding season. Plus, wine expert Toni Osoba has the very best in summer sparkles, and we hear from one woman who gave up her job as a nurse to become a farmer - and she joins us with three of her impressive Highland cows.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: Ainsley gets cosy in the kitchen with some recipes to warm the cockles of your heart. Knocking up dishes that feel like a hug, Ainsley makes a sumptuous beef stroganoff puff pastry pie and classic bread and butter pudding with a twist. On his Mediterranean adventures, Ainsley takes a stroll through the historic city of Valletta, and Charlotte Dawson pops in for a taste of Ainsley's warming penne con pollo.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: Despite Jamie's best efforts on the pitch, his new Italian side are struggling to get a win and stay out of the relegation zone. Things go from bad to worse when the Vardys' lakeside villa is dramatically burgled, leaving the whole family on edge and considering whether to return home. Becky and the kids escape to the mountains for a much-needed change of scenery and time to think clearly about their situation. On a whistle-stop trip back to the UK, Becky and Jamie stage an elaborate photoshoot but also find a quiet moment to make the big decision: whatever happens with the football, they will bring the kids home. On Easter Sunday in Italy, Becky and Jamie reveal their decision to the kids during an Easter Egg hunt to an overwhelming reaction. Shortly after, Becky and Jamie fly the kids back to the UK, arriving home for an emotional reunion with family and friends. But when the season is over, will Jamie be joining them for good or stay in Italy - or will a whole new adventure begin?

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: Despite Jamie's best efforts on the pitch, his new Italian side are struggling to get a win and stay out of the relegation zone. Things go from bad to worse when the Vardys' lakeside villa is dramatically burgled, leaving the whole family on edge and considering whether to return home. Becky and the kids escape to the mountains for a much-needed change of scenery and time to think clearly about their situation. On a whistle-stop trip back to the UK, Becky and Jamie stage an elaborate photoshoot but also find a quiet moment to make the big decision: whatever happens with the football, they will bring the kids home. On Easter Sunday in Italy, Becky and Jamie reveal their decision to the kids during an Easter Egg hunt to an overwhelming reaction. Shortly after, Becky and Jamie fly the kids back to the UK, arriving home for an emotional reunion with family and friends. But when the season is over, will Jamie be joining them for good or stay in Italy - or will a whole new adventure begin?

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot travels to Letterkenny in Donegal, often called Ireland's 'forgotten county', but quickly discovers a place full of unforgettable people, stories and food. Surrounded by ancient rainforest, he heads into the woods to forage for prized golden chanterelle mushrooms before visiting the renowned Lemon Tree Restaurant, where he learns to make tortellini completely from scratch with one of Donegal's most skilled chefs. Dermot also meets Abdul, a Syrian refugee-turned-honey farmer, who teaches him how to extract honey from the hive and shares traditions from home, including how Syrians enjoy honey with strong coffee and a sweet dish called knaffe. Along the way, Dermot uncovers a county quietly building one of Ireland's most exciting food scenes, shaped by resilience, creativity and a deep connection to the land.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Arriving in Derry at the end of the Causeway Coastal Route, Dermot finds a city rewriting its story, with the River Foyle as its beating heart. At the Walled City Brewery - once Army Barracks during the Troubles - he uncovers a secret local ingredient behind their standout brews. For a fresh perspective, Dermot hits the water with kayak instructor Michelle, paddling the Foyle and taking in the skyline from a whole new angle - equal parts scenic and splashy. Back on land, things get fiery on a double-decker bus-turned-taco joint. At Pyke 'N' Pommes, local legend Kevin Pyke blends bold Mexican flavours with top-notch Irish seafood. Dermot gets hands-on, prepping calamari and building tasty tacos that capture Derry's evolving food scene.

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: Despite Jamie's best efforts on the pitch, his new Italian side are struggling to get a win and stay out of the relegation zone. Things go from bad to worse when the Vardys' lakeside villa is dramatically burgled, leaving the whole family on edge and considering whether to return home. Becky and the kids escape to the mountains for a much-needed change of scenery and time to think clearly about their situation. On a whistle-stop trip back to the UK, Becky and Jamie stage an elaborate photoshoot but also find a quiet moment to make the big decision: whatever happens with the football, they will bring the kids home. On Easter Sunday in Italy, Becky and Jamie reveal their decision to the kids during an Easter Egg hunt to an overwhelming reaction. Shortly after, Becky and Jamie fly the kids back to the UK, arriving home for an emotional reunion with family and friends. But when the season is over, will Jamie be joining them for good or stay in Italy - or will a whole new adventure begin?

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot travels to Letterkenny in Donegal, often called Ireland's 'forgotten county', but quickly discovers a place full of unforgettable people, stories and food. Surrounded by ancient rainforest, he heads into the woods to forage for prized golden chanterelle mushrooms before visiting the renowned Lemon Tree Restaurant, where he learns to make tortellini completely from scratch with one of Donegal's most skilled chefs. Dermot also meets Abdul, a Syrian refugee-turned-honey farmer, who teaches him how to extract honey from the hive and shares traditions from home, including how Syrians enjoy honey with strong coffee and a sweet dish called knaffe. Along the way, Dermot uncovers a county quietly building one of Ireland's most exciting food scenes, shaped by resilience, creativity and a deep connection to the land.

programme.desc: Arriving in Derry at the end of the Causeway Coastal Route, Dermot finds a city rewriting its story, with the River Foyle as its beating heart. At the Walled City Brewery - once Army Barracks during the Troubles - he uncovers a secret local ingredient behind their standout brews. For a fresh perspective, Dermot hits the water with kayak instructor Michelle, paddling the Foyle and taking in the skyline from a whole new angle - equal parts scenic and splashy. Back on land, things get fiery on a double-decker bus-turned-taco joint. At Pyke 'N' Pommes, local legend Kevin Pyke blends bold Mexican flavours with top-notch Irish seafood. Dermot gets hands-on, prepping calamari and building tasty tacos that capture Derry's evolving food scene.

programme.desc: Drama based on the novel by Ann Cleeves. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Arriving in Derry at the end of the Causeway Coastal Route, Dermot finds a city rewriting its story, with the River Foyle as its beating heart. At the Walled City Brewery - once Army Barracks during the Troubles - he uncovers a secret local ingredient behind their standout brews. For a fresh perspective, Dermot hits the water with kayak instructor Michelle, paddling the Foyle and taking in the skyline from a whole new angle - equal parts scenic and splashy. Back on land, things get fiery on a double-decker bus-turned-taco joint. At Pyke 'N' Pommes, local legend Kevin Pyke blends bold Mexican flavours with top-notch Irish seafood. Dermot gets hands-on, prepping calamari and building tasty tacos that capture Derry's evolving food scene.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: Dermot travels to Letterkenny in Donegal, often called Ireland's 'forgotten county', but quickly discovers a place full of unforgettable people, stories and food. Surrounded by ancient rainforest, he heads into the woods to forage for prized golden chanterelle mushrooms before visiting the renowned Lemon Tree Restaurant, where he learns to make tortellini completely from scratch with one of Donegal's most skilled chefs. Dermot also meets Abdul, a Syrian refugee-turned-honey farmer, who teaches him how to extract honey from the hive and shares traditions from home, including how Syrians enjoy honey with strong coffee and a sweet dish called knaffe. Along the way, Dermot uncovers a county quietly building one of Ireland's most exciting food scenes, shaped by resilience, creativity and a deep connection to the land.

Retired CIA agent Bryan Mills invites his teenage daughter Kim and his ex-wife Lenore, who has separated from her second husband, to spend a couple of days in Istanbul where he is working - meanwhile, Murad Krasniqi, the patriarch of the Albanian gang of human trafficking broken by Bryan, seeks revenge for the death of his son and organises another gang to kidnap him and his family. When Kim escapes the abductors, she becomes her family's only hope of survival...

programme.title: The Vardys
programme.desc: Despite Jamie's best efforts on the pitch, his new Italian side are struggling to get a win and stay out of the relegation zone. Things go from bad to worse when the Vardys' lakeside villa is dramatically burgled, leaving the whole family on edge and considering whether to return home. Becky and the kids escape to the mountains for a much-needed change of scenery and time to think clearly about their situation. On a whistle-stop trip back to the UK, Becky and Jamie stage an elaborate photoshoot but also find a quiet moment to make the big decision: whatever happens with the football, they will bring the kids home. On Easter Sunday in Italy, Becky and Jamie reveal their decision to the kids during an Easter Egg hunt to an overwhelming reaction. Shortly after, Becky and Jamie fly the kids back to the UK, arriving home for an emotional reunion with family and friends. But when the season is over, will Jamie be joining them for good or stay in Italy - or will a whole new adventure begin?
